en: to confine (to a narrow scope); to limit to

examples.ko: 이번 조사는 서울에 사는 학생으로 국한했어요.
examples.en: This survey was limited to students living in Seoul.

examples.ko: 질문은 오늘 배운 내용으로 국한해 주세요.
examples.en: Please limit your questions to what we learned today.
Don't confine the scope too narrowly.
We decided to limit the presentation to ten minutes.

examples.ko: 연구를 한 가지 문제에 국한한 것이 아쉬워요.
examples.en: It's a pity that the research was confined to one problem.

examples.ko: 우리는 대화를 업무 이야기로 국한할 필요가 없어요.
examples.en: We don't need to limit our conversation to work talk.

explain: '국한되다'는 저절로 범위가 정해지는 것이고 '국한하다'는 사람이 일부러 범위를 정하는 것이에요. '~로 국한하다'처럼 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '~만 하다'로 간단히 말해요.
explain_en: 국한되다 is the range settling on its own, while 국한하다 is a person setting the range on purpose. Use it like ~로 국한하다. In daily talk people simply say ~만 하다.

examples.ko: 그 계획은 눈가림에 불과하다는 비판을 받았어요.
examples.en: The plan was criticized as nothing more than a cover-up.

examples.ko: 눈가림식으로 청소하지 말고 제대로 해 주세요.
examples.en: Please clean properly instead of doing it just for show.

examples.ko: 회사는 눈가림만 하고 문제를 해결하지 않았어요.
examples.en: The company only put on a show and didn't solve the problem.
A showy cover-up gets found out quickly.

examples.ko: 숙제를 눈가림으로 대충 해 가면 선생님이 알아요.
examples.en: If you do your homework carelessly just for show, the teacher will know.
The news used the phrase 'cosmetic construction work'.

explain: 겉만 꾸미고 속은 고치지 않는다는 비판의 느낌이 있어요. '눈가림식', '눈가림 공사'처럼 뒤에 붙여 쓰기도 해요. '눈속임'과 비슷한데 '눈속임'은 마술처럼 눈을 속이는 장면에도 써요.
explain_en: It carries a critical feel of only polishing the surface without fixing what is inside. It is also attached to other words, as in '눈가림식' and '눈가림 공사'. It is similar to '눈속임', but '눈속임' can also describe a trick on the eyes, like in magic.

examples.en: Our team started a counterattack in the second half.
The other team's counterattack was scary.
He fought back against the criticism with words.
Don't miss the chance to counterattack.
In the movie, the hero finally begins to fight back.
The counterattack worked and turned the score around.

explain: '반격'은 공격을 받던 쪽이 되받아 공격하는 것이에요. 스포츠, 전쟁, 토론에서 쓰고 '반격하다', '반격에 나서다'로 자주 말해요. 말로 되받아칠 때는 '반박'과 가깝지만, 반격이 더 싸우는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: 반격 is when the side being attacked hits back. It appears in sports, war and debate as '반격하다' or '반격에 나서다'. In arguments it is close to '반박', but 반격 feels more like a fight.

examples.ko: 올해 농사는 비 때문에 반타작이 됐어요.
examples.en: This year's harvest came out at only about half because of the rain.

examples.ko: 시험 준비를 못 해서 점수가 반타작이에요.
examples.en: I couldn't prepare for the exam, so I only got about half the score.
I'd be glad to finish even half of what I planned.
I think it's fortunate we at least got half.
This round of business ended up at only about half of what I hoped.
Even a half harvest is enough for my family to eat.

explain: 원래는 지주와 소작인이 거둔 곡식을 절반씩 나누는 일을 가리켰고, 지금은 농사나 일, 점수가 절반쯤밖에 안 될 때도 써요. 대체로 '기대보다 아쉽다'는 느낌이 들어 있어요. '반타작이 되다/하다'처럼 말하고 대화에서 편하게 나와요.
explain_en: It originally meant landlord and tenant splitting the harvest in half, and now it is also used when a harvest, work or score reaches only about half. It usually carries a sense of disappointment compared with expectations. It is said as '반타작이 되다/하다' and comes up easily in conversation.

examples.ko: 요즘 바빠서 밥도 변변히 못 먹어요.
examples.en: I'm so busy these days that I can't even eat a decent meal.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 학교도 변변히 다니지 못했어요.
examples.en: As a child, I couldn't even attend school properly.
I'm sorry I couldn't even treat you properly.
We couldn't even pay a decent salary.

examples.ko: 방이 좁아서 변변히 앉을 자리도 없어요.
examples.en: The room is small, so there isn't even a proper place to sit.
I caught a cold and couldn't even rest properly.

explain: 보통 '못', '않다' 같은 부정 표현과 함께 써서 '제대로 못 하다'라는 아쉬움을 나타내요. 일상에서는 '제대로'로 바꿔도 비슷해요.
explain_en: It is usually paired with negatives like '못' or '않다' to express the regret of not being able to do something properly. In daily speech, '제대로' works as a similar replacement.

en: with much trouble; with great pains

examples.ko: 일껏 만들어 놓았는데 아무도 안 먹어요.
examples.en: I went to all the trouble of making it, and nobody is eating it.

examples.ko: 일껏 청소했더니 아이가 금방 어질러 놓았어요.
examples.en: I went to the trouble of cleaning, and my kid made a mess right away.

examples.ko: 일껏 시간을 내서 갔는데 가게가 문을 닫았어요.
examples.en: I made time and made the trip, but the shop was closed.

examples.ko: 일껏 도와줬는데 고맙다는 말도 안 해요.
examples.en: I went out of my way to help, and they don't even say thank you.
The presentation I worked hard to prepare was canceled, and I felt empty.

examples.ko: 일껏 예약까지 했는데 비 때문에 못 갔어요.
examples.en: I even made a reservation, but I couldn't go because of the rain.

explain: 뒤에 '~했는데/했더니'가 이어져서 애쓴 일이 소용없어졌다는 아쉬움을 나타내요. '모처럼'과 비슷하지만 '일껏'은 결과가 안 좋을 때 주로 쓰고, '모처럼'은 좋은 기회에도 써요.
explain_en: It is followed by '~했는데/했더니' and expresses regret that your effort went to waste. It is similar to '모처럼', but '일껏' is mainly for when the result turns out badly, while '모처럼' can also be used for a good opportunity.

examples.en: What nonsense are you talking?
Everything that person says is nonsense.
Stop talking nonsense and just tell me the facts.
I had a high fever and talked deliriously all night.

examples.ko: 그런 소문을 믿다니, 그건 헛소리에 불과해요.
examples.en: How can you believe that rumor? It's nothing but nonsense.
My friend laughed and said I was talking nonsense again.

explain: 말투가 꽤 거칠어서 윗사람이나 처음 만난 사람에게는 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요. 친한 사이에서는 '말도 안 되는 소리'를 가볍게 놀릴 때도 써요. 열이 심할 때 정신없이 하는 말도 '헛소리'라고 해요.
explain_en: The tone is rough, so avoid it with elders or people you've just met. Among close friends it can be a light tease for 'that makes no sense'. It also describes the incoherent talk of someone with a high fever.
